items.good: The maintainer finds, in the same place in every file, what each module is for (its docstring at the top), what each function takes in, gives back and when it stops (type hints and a docstring, the test helpers help_text, help_block, in_one_line and table_rows included), and what each test checks (its name as one sentence, its body as Given/When/Then comments).

Whoever runs the tool gets the same listing on any macOS or Linux machine with Python 3.10 or later and nothing else: only the standard library is imported, nothing newer than 3.10 is used, the package has no dependencies and requires-python >=3.10, and the workflow runs the tests on 3.10 and the latest Python on both systems.

Each stop is one line on standard error after the command's name, naming the path or settings file and its condition (does not exist, is not a folder, cannot be read with the system's reason, names no download folder, names home itself) and what to do: give the folder to organize last as `organize-downloads <folder>`, or check read permission. Giving a real folder clears every one. Tried on the built command: a missing path, a home with no user-dirs file, and a folder with mode 000.

parts.good: What the file is for, and why setuptools>=77, >=3.10 and no dependencies, beside each line.
What the package does and that the command starts in cli.main.
Each function says what it takes, gives and when it stops; main's stop adds what to do to Folder finder's condition; _shown says how names are escaped, by ascii() for characters that cannot be shown.
FolderNotFound says its message holds the path and condition and that the command line adds what to do, as it names the command; the regular expression and each stop are told.
The table is fixed and kept here alone; each constant and function says what it holds or gives.
Why planning is apart from moving, what is left in place, why the result is sorted, and the OSError stop.
Why both systems and two Pythons, why fail-fast is off, why pipx and why src.

The module says it covers output, names, stops and --help, and that the planner or the system's name is replaced only where a test says why; each test name says the behavior; HELP_WIDTH and each help helper say what they are.
Each stop test's name and Then say which condition the stop names.
Only what pipx and uv need to build and put the command on PATH.
Only the listing run: one optional folder argument; --apply and undo wait for T4 and T5.
Each branch serves AC6 or the Linux stop decided in T3.2.
The AC3 table, AC5's endings and the two lookups the planner uses.
One function with the conditions AC5 asks.
One job: install with pipx and run the tests on the matrix AC7 and the 3.10 decision ask.
Each test holds one behavior the code has: the listing's exact lines, singular count, no-file line, system's way, each stop's text, each escape partition, and each section and layout rule of --help.
Each test holds one rule of the folder decision and the exact condition its stop names.

items.good: The command's name is now written once in the code, cli.PROGRAM, used for argparse's prog, before every stop and in the action Folder finder's stops end with; folder.py no longer names the command (pyproject.toml names the console script, which it must). The type table is in type_table alone and the help is written from it; the tests take expected values from tests/__init__.py; build/, *.egg-info/ and __pycache__/ are ignored (git check-ignore confirms).

Each test holds one behavior: the help is checked section by section, its layout in two tests of their own; the system's name is handed by mock, so the test of each system's way gives the same result on any machine; each test makes its own temporary folder, removed after it, and needs no other test first. The task's test command and the workflow's command both pass, 65 tests.
The whole run takes under a tenth of a second (65 tests in 0.09 s), and mutation testing of all 272 mutants ended in about a minute; no new test runs another program.
A listing run only reads: it writes no file, port or folder, so two runs at once, or two test workers each in its own temporary folder, cannot meet.

questions.question: Mutation testing with mutmut (run through uv on a copy, test_stories.py left out) now kills 270 of 272 mutants; statement and branch coverage is 100%. The two left change no behavior: organize.py line 37 `entry.is_file(follow_symlinks=False)` made `follow_symlinks=None` (None counts as false just the same), and type_table.py line 39 `""` for a name with no dot made `"XXXX"` (both go to Others and neither is a downloading ending, as no extension in the table is "xxxx"). No test can fail on either, and B-6 asks that a mutant left out has beside it what the user decided and why. May the run leave these two, with a one-line comment beside each line saying no behavior changes with that mutant and why?
questions.recommended: Yes, a one-line comment beside each of the two lines, since no test can tell these mutants apart from the code and the comment keeps the next maintainer from taking them for a gap.

chosen.chosen: The unreadable-folder test makes a real folder with mode 000 and is skipped when run as root.
chosen.why: It checks the true path from os.scandir through the planner to the stop; root reads any folder, and GitHub Actions does not run as root.

chosen.chosen: The invalid-byte test hands the planner's result (a name decoded from b"bad\xff.pdf") in place of the planner.
chosen.why: macOS's file system refuses a file name that is not valid UTF-8, and AC7 asks the tests to hold on both systems.

chosen.chosen: A broken symbolic link given as the folder counts as 'is not a folder', and a link to a folder is organized; both held by tests.
chosen.why: That is what the code does (os.path.lexists), and the link itself is there; the tests keep the decision's rules from changing unnoticed.

chosen.chosen: Folder finder's stops hold the path and condition only; cli adds 'give the folder to organize last: organize-downloads <folder>' from PROGRAM.
chosen.why: So the command's name is written in one place in the code, as the B-5 send-back asked; the stops the user sees are word for word as before.

chosen.chosen: Characters that cannot be shown are escaped with ascii(char)[1:-1] in place of encode('unicode_escape').decode('ascii').
chosen.why: It gives the same escapes with no codec names, which mutation testing turned into mutants that change nothing.

chosen.chosen: --help is held by tests of each section's wording (words joined, apart from line breaks), of the extension column two spaces after Installers, and of filling each paragraph and table row to 79 columns; COLUMNS is set to 80 while it runs.
chosen.why: Each section and each layout rule then fails its own test; argparse wraps its own part by the terminal width, so a fixed width keeps the result the same on every machine.

chosen.chosen: The test of each system's way of finding Downloads hands platform.system() 'Darwin' and 'Linux' by mock.
chosen.why: The test then fails on any machine when main stops passing the system's name, rather than only on macOS.
